children: Shares of enterprise technology company Hewlett Packard Enterprise
fell 16.4% in the afternoon session after the company reported sequential declines in GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins in its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results.

According to the company's earnings release, Hewlett Packard Enterprise posted GAAP gross margin of 38.0%, down 210 basis points sequentially, and non-GAAP gross margin of 38.2%, down 220 basis points sequentially, though both increased from the prior-year period. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.43 topped the company's $1.20 to $1.30 outlook range and the consensus estimate of $1.29. The company reported revenue of $14.55 billion, up 50.3% year on year and above the consensus estimate of $14.45 billion, while free cash flow margin fell to 13.2% from 20.1% in the same quarter of the previous year.

Looking ahead, CFO Marie Myers said on the earnings call that the company expects gross margin to moderate "as fiscal 2027 progresses" because of a higher mix of AI servers and "costs increasing faster than pricing." The company also expects memory and NAND supply to remain constrained through at least the second half of calendar 2028.

Lower gross margins and rising component costs can reduce the profit a company earns on each dollar of sales. Share prices often fall when investors worry that a shift in product mix and supply constraints will limit future profitability.
What is the market telling us

Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 43 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Hewlett Packard Enterprise and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock gained 14.8% on the news that Nvidia announced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO, sparking renewed investor confidence across artificial intelligence and semiconductor markets following the previous week's sharp downturn. The leadership news lifted broader market indexes as investors stepped back into artificial intelligence and data center operators, reversing a steep retreat that had recently pushed major market benchmarks into correction territory. A market correction occurs when an index declines by 10 percent or more from its recent peak, underscoring the severity of the prior sell-off. Technology and semiconductor shares led the advance during early trading, signaling that investor sentiment has stabilized across the wider chip ecosystem.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is up 65.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $40.10 per share, it is still trading 45.4% below its 52-week high of $73.46 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,699.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.
